questions.q: Why does the author say social media and author platforms fail new writers?
a: Their benefits only appear at a scale beginners do not yet have
Readers on those channels rarely buy any kind of book
Amazon penalizes authors who promote books elsewhere
They take too much time away from writing quality prose
questions.why: Lesson 1 explains that both have long-term upside but are useless in the short term because they work at scale.

questions.q: What makes a strong Kindle book title, according to the summary?
a: It is short, clear and shows the result within two seconds
It is clever and makes readers pause to work out the meaning
It lists the author’s credentials and publishing history
It uses as many searchable keywords as possible
questions.why: Lesson 2 says Amazon shoppers scan, so a title must be short, clear, attractive and instantly descriptive.

questions.q: What does the author advise about designing your book’s cover?
a: Pay a professional rather than doing it yourself
Design it yourself to save money at the start
Use the same template as other books in your category
Keep it plain so the title stands out instead
questions.why: Lesson 2 is blunt: do not design the cover yourself; spend what you can on a professional.

questions.q: How many good reviews early on can help push a book into its category’s top 10?
a: About five or six in the first few days
At least fifty within the first month
A few hundred spread over a year
Only reviews from verified industry critics count
questions.why: Lesson 3 says just five or six good reviews shortly after launch can take a book to the top 10.

questions.q: What did the two inbox book titles show about naming a book?
a: A title should communicate the end result immediately
A longer title usually ranks better in Amazon search
Puns and wordplay make a book more memorable
The subtitle matters far more than the main title
questions.why: Lesson 2 compares the two titles to show that instant clarity about the outcome wins attention.
